agreement_type.name: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement
agreement_type.description: Mutual NDA exchanged when evaluating a potential commercial relationship. Six fictional negotiations: four on our paper, two on counterparty paper.

entries.label: Parties & Recitals
entries.description: Who is bound; mutual vs one-way framing; Discloser/Recipient defined terms.

entries.label: Term
entries.description: Effective date and the period during which disclosures may be made. Distinct from how long the confidentiality duty survives.

entries.label: Non-Solicitation of Employees
entries.description: No-hire/no-solicit of personnel met through the evaluation; general-advertising and unsolicited-applicant carve-outs.

entries.label: No License / IP Ownership
entries.description: Disclosure conveys no licence and no ownership; each party retains its own IP.

entries.label: Limitation of Liability
entries.description: Usually ABSENT from a mutual NDA — flag loudly if a counterparty introduces one, since capping breach-of-confidence damages guts the agreement's only real remedy.

entries.label: Governing Law
entries.description: Which jurisdiction's law governs.

entries.label: Assignment
entries.description: Consent to assign; affiliate and change-of-control carve-outs.

entries.label: Purpose & Permitted Use
entries.description: The defined Purpose, and the covenant not to use Confidential Information for anything else. Breadth of Purpose is the quietest high-stakes term in an NDA.

entries.label: Definition of Confidential Information
entries.description: What counts as Confidential Information; whether marking is required, and whether oral disclosures must be reduced to writing within N days.

entries.label: Exclusions from Confidential Information
entries.description: The four standard carve-outs — already known to the recipient without a duty of confidence, independently developed without reference to the other party's information, publicly available through no fault of the recipient, and rightfully received from a third party — plus which party bears the burden of proving them. Removing any of the four is a substantive narrowing, not housekeeping.

entries.label: Permitted Disclosure to Representatives
entries.description: The need-to-know circle (affiliates, employees, advisors); whether Recipient stays liable for its Representatives' breach.

entries.label: Standard of Care
entries.description: Degree of care owed — reasonable care, or same-as-own-but-no-less-than-reasonable.

entries.label: Compelled Disclosure
entries.description: Subpoena / legal-process carve-out; prior-notice and cooperation duties, and whether notice is excused where legally prohibited.

entries.label: Survival of Confidentiality Obligations
entries.description: How long the confidentiality duty runs past the term. The single most-negotiated number in an NDA. A DEFINED, BOUNDED period is required — an obligation with no end date is an unbounded liability, not a stronger protection.

entries.label: Trade Secret Carve-Out
entries.description: Whether trade secrets remain protected past the general survival period, drafted against a condition ('for so long as such information remains a trade secret under applicable law') rather than against perpetuity. See note 2 in the header.

entries.label: Return or Destruction of Materials
entries.description: Return/destroy on demand; carve-outs for automatic backups, archival copies and legal-hold retention.

entries.label: Residuals
entries.description: Whether unaided-memory residual knowledge may be freely used. A residuals clause substantially undercuts the confidentiality duty; frequently proposed by the receiving side.

entries.label: No Warranty / AS IS
entries.description: Confidential Information provided AS IS; no warranty of accuracy or completeness.

entries.label: Confidentiality of the Discussions
entries.description: Whether the existence, terms or status of the discussions themselves are confidential — distinct from protecting the information exchanged. Genuinely negotiated: parties with disclosure obligations of their own resist an unqualified version.

entries.label: Notice of Unauthorized Disclosure
entries.description: Duty to notify the disclosing party promptly on discovering unauthorized use, disclosure or loss, and to cooperate in mitigation.

entries.label: Data Protection / Personal Data
entries.description: Where Confidential Information includes personal data: applicable privacy-law obligations and whether a separate data-processing agreement is required.

entries.label: Export Control
entries.description: Export-control and sanctions compliance for disclosed technical data. Near-universal boilerplate; rarely negotiated.

entries.label: No Obligation to Proceed
entries.description: No binding transaction, no exclusivity, either party may terminate discussions.

entries.label: Injunctive Relief
entries.description: Equitable remedies acknowledged; whether bond and proof of actual damages are waived.

entries.label: Dispute Resolution & Venue
entries.description: Forum and exclusive jurisdiction; arbitration; jury-trial waiver.

entries.label: Notices
entries.description: Notice addresses and method — the channel a return-or-destroy demand travels down.

entries.label: Entire Agreement & Amendment
entries.description: Integration clause and the writing-signed-by-both amendment requirement.

entries.label: Severability
entries.description: Invalid-provision survival; blue-pencilling an overbroad restriction.

entries.label: Counterparts
entries.description: Execution in counterparts; electronic signatures.

entries.label: Most Favored Nation
entries.description: No pricing in an NDA.

entries.label: Non-Compete
entries.description: A true non-compete does not belong in an NDA; activate and escalate if one appears.

entries.label: Exclusivity
entries.description: NDAs are expressly non-exclusive — see no_obligation_to_proceed.

entries.label: No-Solicit of Customers
entries.description: Occasionally smuggled in; activate and escalate if one appears.

entries.label: License Grant
entries.description: An NDA grants no licence by design; the express no-licence statement classifies under no_license_ip_ownership.

entries.label: Minimum Commitment
entries.description: Nothing is committed — evaluation only.

entries.label: Price Restrictions
entries.description: No pricing terms.

entries.label: Revenue/Profit Sharing
entries.description: No commercial terms.

entries.label: Audit Rights
entries.description: A right to inspect Recipient's systems is an overreach in an NDA; activate and escalate if one appears.

entries.label: Insurance
entries.description: Not applicable.

entries.label: Warranty Duration
entries.description: Not applicable — see no_warranty_as_is.

entries.label: Change of Control
entries.description: Handled as a carve-out inside assignment.

entries.label: Third-Party Beneficiary
entries.description: NDAs disclaim third-party beneficiaries; not separately tracked.

entries.label: Post-Termination Services
entries.description: No services are provided under an NDA.

our_standard.text: Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets.

If Recipient is required by law or legal process to disclose Confidential Information, it shall, where legally permitted, give Discloser prompt written notice so that Discloser may seek a protective order, and shall disclose only that portion legally required.

Neither party shall disclose the existence or status of the discussions between the parties without the other party's prior written consent, except as required by law or by the rules of a securities exchange.
This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one agreement.

"Confidential Information" means non-public information disclosed by Discloser that is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances of disclosure. Information disclosed orally need not be reduced to writing in order to be protected.
The state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of this Agreement, and each party submits to that jurisdiction.
This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties as to its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions. It may be amended only by a writing signed by both parties.

Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) was already known to Recipient without a duty of confidentiality; (b) was independently developed by Recipient without reference to or use of Discloser's Confidential Information; (c) is or becomes publicly available through no act or omission of Recipient; or (d) is rightfully received by Recipient from a third party without a duty of confidentiality. Recipient bears the burden of establishing that an exclusion applies.
Each party shall comply with applicable export control and sanctions laws with respect to any technical data disclosed under this Agreement.
This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

Each party acknowledges that a breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are an inadequate remedy, and that the non-breaching party is entitled to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity.

No license or other right in any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property is granted by this Agreement or by any disclosure made under it. Each party retains all right, title, and interest in its own Confidential Information.

Nothing in this Agreement obligates either party to proceed with any transaction, grants either party exclusivity, or restricts either party from pursuing similar discussions with third parties. Either party may terminate discussions at any time.
All Confidential Information is provided AS IS. Neither party makes any representation or warranty as to the accuracy or completeness of any Confidential Information it discloses.

Recipient shall notify Discloser promptly upon discovering any unauthorized use, disclosure, or loss of Confidential Information, and shall cooperate reasonably with Discloser to mitigate its effects.
Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and sent to the addresses set out beneath the parties' signatures, and are effective on receipt.

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by and between AlphaCorp Holdings, Inc. ("AlphaCorp") and [Counterparty] ("Counterparty"). Each party may disclose information to the other in connection with the Purpose, and each party may act as both a disclosing party ("Discloser") and a receiving party ("Recipient").

Recipient may disclose Confidential Information only to its employees, affiliates, and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement ("Representatives"). Recipient remains responsible for any breach by its Representatives.
The "Purpose" is the evaluation of a potential commercial relationship between the parties. Recipient shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and for no other purpose.

Upon Discloser's written request, Recipient shall return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession and, if requested, certify that it has done so. Recipient may retain copies held in routine automated backups and copies it is required to retain by law or legal hold, which remain subject to this Agreement for as long as they are retained.
If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and the remaining provisions continue in full force.
Recipient shall protect Confidential Information using reasonable care.
Recipient's obligations with respect to Confidential Information continue for three (3) years from the date of its disclosure, notwithstanding any expiration or termination of this Agreement.

This Agreement takes effect on the date of last signature and continues for two (2) years, unless earlier terminated by either party on thirty (30) days written notice. Disclosures may be made only during this period.

posture.system_prompt: Rounds before escalating: Typically two rounds of redlines before we escalate to outside counsel or walk; our own history shows most deals settle by the second or third version. Default leverage posture: Collaborative — four of our six negotiated NDAs closed on our own paper and most changes were accepted without escalation; we lead from our standard form but do not force it through unchanged. Non-material counterparty change: We accept non-material redlines (venue, governing law, notice mechanics, minor wording) to keep a deal moving, but hold firm on the two clause types named above and never accept a limitation-of-liability clause that reaches a confidentiality breach. Hard lines named in interview (see Floor): Exclusions from Confidential Information; Survival of Confidentiality Obligations. Flexible to close a deal: Governing law, dispute resolution venue, and standard of care — our history shows these move to a counterparty's preferred jurisdiction or phrasing without us treating it as a loss. Output audience and deal-size sensitivity: Terse — reviewed by in-house counsel who already knows the standard form, not a first-time reader.

interview.question: How many negotiation rounds do you typically go on this agreement type before escalating or walking?
interview.answer: Typically two rounds of redlines before we escalate to outside counsel or walk; our own history shows most deals settle by the second or third version.

interview.question: What's your default leverage posture? (take-it-or-leave-it standard form / collaborative / we usually need the deal more than they do)
interview.answer: Collaborative — four of our six negotiated NDAs closed on our own paper and most changes were accepted without escalation; we lead from our standard form but do not force it through unchanged.

interview.question: When a counterparty change is non-material, do you default to accept-to-close, or hold the line?
interview.answer: We accept non-material redlines (venue, governing law, notice mechanics, minor wording) to keep a deal moving, but hold firm on the two clause types named above and never accept a limitation-of-liability clause that reaches a confidentiality breach.

interview.question: Which clause types are non-negotiable regardless of deal value?
interview.answer: Exclusions from Confidential Information; Survival of Confidentiality Obligations

interview.question: Which clause types are you happy to concede to move a deal?
interview.answer: Governing law, dispute resolution venue, and standard of care — our history shows these move to a counterparty's preferred jurisdiction or phrasing without us treating it as a loss.

interview.question: Who will read the output, and does anything change above a deal-value threshold? (GC audience, terse rationale, no change by deal size / GC audience, terse rationale, but tightens above a threshold — say what threshold / junior-reviewer audience, needs it explained, no change by deal size / junior-reviewer audience, needs it explained, and tightens above a threshold — say what threshold)
interview.answer: Terse — reviewed by in-house counsel who already knows the standard form, not a first-time reader.

invariants.statement: Limitation of liability, if present, must not apply to a breach of the confidentiality obligations in this Agreement.
invariants.rationale: A $50,000 liability cap appeared in 3 of 6 deals (epsilon-systems, theta-logistics, zeta-diagnostics) -- introduced by the counterparty in theta-logistics and zeta-diagnostics (both counterparty-paper) and carried into our own epsilon-systems draft; our taxonomy flags limitation-of-liability as normally absent from a mutual NDA because capping breach-of-confidence damages guts the agreement's only real remedy.
